articles.headline: Lugo es el área sanitaria con más consultas e ingresos por gripe de Galicia
articles.subtitle: La incidencia alcanza las 23 consultas por cada 100.000 habitantes, frente a las cuatro de Ferrol o las ocho de Pontevedra, y sube un 53% en una semana. Los médicos del PAC reclaman un refuerzo extra para San Froilán.
articles.body:
Lugo es el área sanitaria gallega con la tasa más elevada de consultas y de ingresos hospitalarios por gripe, según los datos semanales que publica Sanidade. La incidencia se sitúa en 23 consultas por cada 100.000 habitantes, frente a las cuatro de Ferrol, las ocho de Pontevedra o las 7,2 de Ourense, y en solo una semana ha subido un 53%.

Los ingresos, 2,8 por cada 100.000, casi triplican los de la mayoría de áreas gallegas, que no llegan ni a uno.

El covid también está elevando la presión asistencial en Primaria y en el hospital, pero es la gripe el virus que más está afectando a los lucenses. Los cuadros se presentan a menudo con dolor de cabeza y mialgias sin problemas respiratorios, además de fiebre y síntomas digestivos, y Sanidade recomienda reposo, mascarilla y lavado de manos frecuente.

## El PAC reclama refuerzos para las patronales

Los médicos del Punto de Atención Continuada (PAC) de Lugo denuncian que este año, por primera vez, no contarán con un equipo adicional de facultativo y enfermería durante el San Froilán, cuando las patronales coinciden con la mayor circulación de virus del otoño. Sanidade recuerda que en junio se consolidó un cuarto equipo, reclamado durante años, pero que no cubre las noches ni los viernes.

El centro de urgencias de Primaria dispone ahora de unos 60 test de antígenos al mes para hacer la prueba in situ a pacientes seleccionados. Con las comidas familiares de las fiestas por delante, en el área sanitaria temen que los casos crezcan de forma exponencial en la tercera y cuarta semana de octubre.

articles.headline: Lugo vuelve a la calle este sábado por la vivienda con una concentración ante el Concello
articles.subtitle: La asociación Mádia leva convoca a las 19:00 en la Praza Maior, tras la protesta del martes, que reunió a más de un centenar de personas. En Santiago, la acampada del Obradoiro cumple su tercera noche.
articles.body:
Lugo será escenario este sábado de una nueva concentración en defensa del derecho a una vivienda digna, convocada por la asociación Mádia leva para las 19:00 horas en la Praza Maior, frente al Concello. La cita llega después de la protesta del martes, en la que más de un centenar de personas se congregaron en el mismo lugar con el respaldo de la CIG, Vivenda Xa!, Galiza Nova, Erguer y la coordinadora da mocidade socialista.

La convocatoria responde al rechazo del Congreso a los decretos de vivienda, que incluían la prohibición de desahucios para personas en situación de vulnerabilidad y la extensión de los contratos de alquiler con vencimiento este año. La votación arrojó 172 votos a favor, de PSOE, Sumar, ERC, Bildu, PNV, Podemos, BNG, CC y Compromís, y 178 en contra, de PP, Vox, Junts y UPN.

## Marchas en toda Galicia

Las movilizaciones del fin de semana forman parte de una oleada convocada en toda Galicia. En Vigo, la Alianza pola Vivenda ha fijado una manifestación a las 19:00 desde el cruce de Vía Norte con Urzáiz hasta la Porta do Sol.

En A Coruña, el Sindicato de Vivenda sale a la misma hora desde Ronda de Outeiro bajo el lema «Contra el rentismo, por la huelga general». En Pontevedra habrá concentración el lunes a las 20:00 en la Praza da Peregrina.

En Santiago de Compostela, la acampada por la vivienda de la Praza do Obradoiro cumple su tercera noche y sus participantes prevén sumarse a una concentración este sábado a las 12:00 en el mismo lugar. «Cada día somos más», declaró la portavoz de la asamblea, Eirena Souto.

articles.headline: La caída de los decretos de vivienda deja la legislatura en el aire y Sánchez se toma el fin de semana para decidir
articles.subtitle: Moncloa asegura que no descarta ningún escenario y espera ver «cómo respira la calle» este sábado, con manifestaciones en más de 50 ciudades. Feijóo le pide que disuelva las Cortes y convoque elecciones.
articles.body:
La caída de los dos decretos de vivienda en el Congreso ha asestado un golpe que Moncloa admite que puede resultar definitivo para la legislatura. El presidente Pedro Sánchez, único con potestad para convocar elecciones generales, se ha dado el fin de semana para reflexionar, según fuentes gubernamentales, que no descartan ningún escenario y que quieren tomar el pulso de la calle.

Junts confirmó el jueves que votaría en contra y desde entonces los rumores de adelanto electoral sobrevolaron los pasillos del Congreso. El propio Sánchez los alimentó en su intervención por sorpresa: «La historia les juzgará antes de lo que creen y con mayor contundencia de lo que imaginan».

## «Lo veremos en las urnas»

El Gobierno dirige ahora el foco hacia el PP y Junts. Fuentes gubernamentales sostienen que no midieron las consecuencias de tumbar unas medidas que iban a amortiguar el principal problema del país y avisan de que esa decisión les pasará factura: «Lo veremos en las urnas». El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, le ha lanzado el guante inverso: «Tiene la coartada, ponga la fecha, disuelva las Cortes, convoque elecciones y que hablen los españoles».

La ministra de Vivienda había pedido a Junts que se abstuviera y ofreció tramitar los decretos como proyecto de ley para incorporar cambios, sin éxito. Con las quinielas electorales abiertas, Moncloa quiere medir primero la respuesta de la calle: este sábado hay convocadas manifestaciones por la vivienda en más de 50 ciudades.

articles.headline: Una riada deja una muerta de 102 años y 90 rescatados en Madrigueras
articles.subtitle: El municipio albaceteño registró 142 litros por metro cuadrado y el agua superó el metro dentro de algunas viviendas. Castilla-La Mancha elevó el Meteocam a nivel 1 y envió un ES-Alert a La Manchuela.
articles.body:
Una mujer de 102 años ha fallecido y 90 personas han tenido que ser rescatadas este viernes en Madrigueras (Albacete) después de una riada que inundó toda la localidad. El municipio registró 142 litros por metro cuadrado y el agua alcanzó una altura superior al metro en el interior de algunas viviendas.

Según la Junta de Castilla-La Mancha, los servicios de emergencia realizaron alrededor de 90 rescates, sobre todo de personas atrapadas en casas anegadas. La concejala María Victoria Leal sitúa el inicio de las inundaciones a las 18:00, con «medio metro de agua» en las calles, coches arrastrados y numerosos vecinos «asustados y sin saber cómo actuar».

## Alertas en una quincena de comunidades

El Gobierno regional envió un ES-Alert a las 19:36 a la comarca de La Manchuela albaceteña y a parte de la conquense para recomendar que se evitaran los desplazamientos, y a las 22:15 elevó el Meteocam a nivel 1 en Albacete. La Unidad de Seguridad Ciudadana de la Guardia Civil permaneció desplegada durante la madrugada y esta mañana se incorpora un equipo de Geacam para reforzar la limpieza y la recuperación de las zonas afectadas.

La misma jornada, una tromba de agua dejó 97 litros por metro cuadrado en una sola hora en Alzira (Valencia), y las lluvias y tormentas mantienen en alerta a una quincena de comunidades autónomas en las próximas horas.

articles.headline: El Sindicato de Inquilinas llama a la huelga general y convoca protestas en más de 50 ciudades
articles.subtitle: La confederación llama a salir este sábado, con la marcha principal en Madrid a las 12:00 y cuatro columnas. En la Puerta del Sol, cientos de acampados desafían la lluvia: «No nos vamos».
articles.body:
La Confederación de Sindicatos de Inquilinas ha convocado manifestaciones en más de 50 ciudades españolas para este sábado y ha anunciado que «el siguiente paso es la huelga general». La organización sostiene que el Congreso ha mostrado una «absoluta insensibilidad, falta de empatía y sordera» ante las demandas de la calle y que bloquear los decretos de vivienda «debe tener un coste político».

La marcha principal será en Madrid a las 12:00, con cuatro columnas que partirán de la glorieta de Emilio Castelar, Atocha, el Hospital de la Princesa y la Plaza de España. Entre las demás convocatorias figuran Barcelona, Valencia, Zaragoza, Málaga, Palma de Mallorca, Valladolid y Granada, y la confederación detalla en su web los horarios previstos también para el domingo y el lunes.

## Acampada en la Puerta del Sol

En la Puerta del Sol, cientos de personas mantienen una acampada que ha resistido la lluvia de las últimas horas. «No nos vamos», corearon los concentrados, decididos a sostener la protesta contra lo que describen como un Congreso «secuestrado por el rentismo».

Los convocantes advierten de que mantendrían las movilizaciones «incluso si las medidas prosperaban», porque las consideraban «parches y reformas absolutamente insuficientes», y afirman que van a hacer que quienes den la espalda al pueblo tengan que dejar su sitio en el Parlamento.

articles.headline: El paro juvenil se dispara en septiembre: nueve de cada diez nuevos parados tienen menos de 25 años
articles.subtitle: El desempleo subió en 23.587 personas, hasta 2.379.505, la cifra más baja para un septiembre desde 2007. Pero entre los menores de 25 años creció un 12,77% y la regularización de inmigrantes explica buena parte del repunte.
articles.body:
El paro registrado subió en 23.587 personas en septiembre y se situó en 2.379.505 desempleados, la cifra más baja para ese mes desde 2007, según los datos publicados por los ministerios de Trabajo y Seguridad Social. La subida mensual ha sido, aun así, la más intensa para un septiembre desde 2017.

El desglose muestra el verdadero foco: el paro entre los menores de 25 años aumentó en 21.411 personas, un 12,77%, hasta 189.141 jóvenes. Concentran nueve de cada diez nuevos desempleados y su subida es casi trece veces superior a la del conjunto. El paro entre quienes no tenían empleo anterior creció en 17.966 personas.

## La regularización distorsiona el dato

El Ministerio de Trabajo atribuye buena parte del repunte al proceso extraordinario de regularización de inmigrantes. Al terminar septiembre había 56.476 personas desempleadas inscritas tras acogerse a esa vía, y el 52% llevaba menos de un mes registrado. La afiliación, en cambio, sumó 92.327 cotizantes, de los que unos 83.000 eran extranjeros.

Para el Adecco Group Institute, el paro juvenil es una de las «señales de alerta» del mes. Trabajo prepara una estrategia para captar a los jóvenes que no se inscriben en el Sepe —seis de cada diez parados juveniles no figuran como demandantes— y prevé colocar a 200.000 hasta 2028.

articles.headline: Un 65% de españoles respalda que el Supremo suspendiera la Ley de Nietos
articles.subtitle: El 39,2% cree que la norma podía distorsionar el censo electoral y un 17,9% ve una «limitación injustificada» del voto. Casi la mitad de los votantes del PSOE ve con buenos ojos la medida del tribunal.
articles.body:
El 65,1% de los españoles considera que el Tribunal Supremo hizo bien al suspender cautelarmente la llamada Ley de Nietos, según una encuesta de Sigma Dos para EL MUNDO. La opción mayoritaria, un 39,2%, sostiene que es «una medida necesaria para garantizar la correcta configuración del censo y evitar posibles distorsiones en los próximos procesos electorales».

Un 22,3% la ve como «una medida cautelar razonable mientras se revisan y aclaran los criterios utilizados para la inscripción en el censo». En el lado contrario, un 17,9% considera que supone «una limitación injustificada del derecho al voto de personas que han adquirido legalmente la nacionalidad española», y un 12,8% la lee como una intromisión judicial en una norma aprobada por el legislador.

## Una suspensión que no anula nacionalidades

El Supremo suspendió en septiembre los efectos electorales de la inscripción en el censo de residentes ausentes (CERA) de parte de los nacionalizados por la Ley de Memoria Democrática, a raíz de un recurso de Vox e Iustitia Europa. El tribunal apreció un «peligro fundado» para la transparencia del proceso, pero la medida no anula ninguna nacionalidad concedida y la sala prevé dictar sentencia en diciembre.

El sondeo muestra un electorado dividido: un 45,9% de los votantes del PSOE suscribe alguna de las opciones favorables a la suspensión, mientras que el 69,4% de los de Sumar la rechaza. Entre los mayores de 75 años el respaldo llega al 47,2%, y un 46,9% de los encuestados está «nada» de acuerdo con que personas que no viven en España elijan a sus dirigentes.

articles.headline: Drumcree investigation to start next week, says Robinson, as stand-off drags on
articles.subtitle: The DUP leader says there must be 'consequences' for 'people who are law makers who are acting as law breakers'. Residents' fresh legal challenge is postponed to Monday and no further talks are scheduled.
articles.body:
The leader of the Democratic Unionist Party says he expects the criminal investigation into the unlawful blocking of the Garvaghy Road to begin next week. Gavin Robinson said there had to be «consequences» for «people who are law makers who are acting as law breakers», adding that the inquiry «needs the space to see it conclude as well».

The PSNI chief constable said on Wednesday that there would be an investigation. Protesters remain on the mainly nationalist road outside Portadown, where about 20 people were gathered on Friday morning, while five Orangemen maintained a presence at Drumcree church, about a mile away.

## Talks end without agreement

Four days of talks at Hillsborough Castle ended on Thursday night without a deal. Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant said it was «the end of these conversations» but that his door «remains open». Breándan Mac Cionnaith, of the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition, said there had been no «meeting of minds», and Portadown Orange Order district master Nigel Dawson said the position «remains as it has been».

A fresh legal bid by residents to prevent the march was due to be heard on Friday but has been postponed until Monday. First Minister Michelle O'Neill, who attended the protest, says she understands the law but chose to «stand in solidarity» with residents. Robinson told the News Letter that Sinn Féin had shown a «reckless disregard for devolution and power-sharing».

In a Facebook post, the rector of Drumcree Church, the Reverend Gary Galway, said he had received hundreds of «extremely nasty» emails, texts and calls. Thirteen councillors have been reported to the local government standards watchdog over their conduct in the dispute, which has drawn 25 allegations.

articles.headline: The G7 agrees to release up to 100m barrels of oil and diesel to cool prices
articles.subtitle: The deal came after Donald Trump threatened to ban US diesel exports unless Europe released more of its own stocks. UK pump prices passed £2 a litre for the first time on Friday.
articles.body:
G7 leaders have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in an attempt to ease supply pressures that have pushed fuel prices sharply higher. The group said the move would include a «substantial release» of diesel in the coming days, and the reserves will be released over four months under the coordination of the International Energy Agency.

The joint statement also commits members to «refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products» on one another — a direct answer to Donald Trump's threat to ban US diesel exports if European countries did not put more of their own stocks on the market. «Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately,» Trump posted on Friday.

## Why diesel drives the numbers

Diesel is used heavily by haulage and agriculture, so rises feed straight through into essentials such as food. US refineries produce roughly four to five million barrels a day, Americans consume about 3.6 million of that, and refiners export the remaining 1.2 to 1.5 million — making the US a critical supplier to the global market.

The UK, represented at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, said the measures would «stabilise energy supplies» and shield households and businesses from price shocks. British pump prices topped £2 a litre for the first time on Friday; the 100 million barrels will be a mix of diesel and crude oil.

articles.headline: Riot police clash with students as French school protests spread
articles.subtitle: More than 700 schools were disrupted on Friday and at least 65 staff have been injured. A 17-year-old was arrested in Belfort on suspicion of attempted homicide after a police officer was targeted.
articles.body:
Riot police have clashed with protesters as thousands of students demonstrating over education standards disrupted more than 700 schools in France on Friday. Fires burned in the streets as pupils objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

The protests began last week in Paris and have spread across the country, with Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille among the cities affected. Justice minister Gérald Darmanin said things had «gone from high-school student demonstrations to a public order disturbance», and the education ministry reported at least 65 injured staff members.

Hundreds of arrests have been made. A 17-year-old was arrested on suspicion of attempted homicide after protests in Belfort, north-eastern France, where a police officer was targeted, and police published images of items seized from demonstrators, including petrol bombs, an axe and so-called mortar fireworks. In the Paris suburb of Pantin officers charged at protesters, and tear gas was deployed in Strasbourg.

Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes suffered more than €2m of damage after fire destroyed its glass entrance and parts of the interior, according to the regional government. «It makes us even angrier — the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us», said Lola, a 16-year-old protester.

articles.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as fighting escalates in the north
articles.subtitle: Addis Ababa closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats; Eritrea called the move 'astounding' and severed relations. More than 50 people have been killed since fighting resumed last week.
articles.body:
Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict. Addis Ababa announced on Thursday that it was closing its embassy in Asmara and ordering 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security. Eritrea said it had no option but to reciprocate in kind.

The diplomatic rupture came hours after powerful explosions were heard overnight in Addis Ababa, including near the military headquarters and the intelligence service. A source linked to the opposition alliance told Reuters that its forces had carried out drone attacks in the capital; Ethiopian authorities have not confirmed what caused the blasts.

## A war that never really ended

Federal forces are battling the Tigray People's Liberation Front and its allies across parts of Tigray, Afar and Amhara, and appear to be advancing towards Mekelle. More than 50 people have been killed since the fighting resumed last week — the most serious hostilities since the 2022 peace deal ended a war in which an estimated 600,000 people died.

Last month the TPLF joined six other armed movements, including the Fano militia from Amhara, in an alliance whose stated aim is to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing it; Eritrea's information minister told the BBC Tigrinya that Addis Ababa was deflecting attention from its own conflicts. Relations between the neighbours have soured badly over Ethiopia's push for direct access to the Red Sea.

articles.headline: Russian strikes have left Kyiv in a 'very dramatic situation', mayor warns
articles.subtitle: Vitaliy Klitschko says Moscow is battering critical infrastructure, logistics and housing, and that the capital is fighting for 'survival'. The Pivdennyi bridge was hit four times in two days.
articles.body:
Intensified Russian drone and missile strikes have left Kyiv in a «very dramatic situation», mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said after the city's defence council held a crisis meeting. Moscow is battering «critical infrastructure, logistics, housing» and other key facilities, he said, and the aim is to «sow panic». «We're talking about survival», he added.

Kyiv's key Pivdennyi, or Southern, bridge was hit in an overnight drone attack and struck again on Friday evening — the fourth time in two days. All metro and car traffic is suspended across it and restrictions are in place on the city's two other main bridges, causing major delays. The city's data centres have also been hit recently, causing internet outages.

One person was killed when a multi-storey residential building was hit overnight. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Vladimir Putin had decided in early September that «there are no rules now», describing a campaign against bridges, data centres, hospitals, kindergartens and schools aimed at making people flee.

Putin said the strikes were a response to Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and ships in the Black Sea, and acknowledged Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP as a result. Ukraine says it targets oil infrastructure because it helps fund the war.

articles.headline: Flydubai co-pilot was barred from flying in Oman over extremism suspicions
articles.subtitle: The man suspected of trying to crash an Israel-bound flight had been banned from flying in his home country, the Wall Street Journal reports. Netanyahu claims 'Islamist radicalisation' without producing evidence.
articles.body:
The Flydubai co-pilot accused of trying to crash a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people on board had been barred from flying in his home country of Oman over suspicions that he held extremist views, according to a person familiar with the investigation. The ban was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

He was later hired by the Dubai-based airline. It is not clear how thoroughly his background was checked when he joined the carrier in the United Arab Emirates, where a regional investigation is still open. Investigators are examining whether he acted alone; officials say there is no evidence so far of a link to Iran, even as Donald Trump suggested possible Tehran involvement.

## A region on edge

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the attacker had undergone «Islamist radicalisation», without offering evidence, and vowed that «whoever sent him» would pay a heavy price. Emirati authorities, who are leading the inquiry, have not confirmed the motive.

The attack has plunged regional travel into crisis. The UAE has cancelled all flights to Israel, and the two countries agreed on repatriation flights, which began on Friday, to bring home passengers who were stranded in the Emirates after commercial connections between them were suspended.

articles.headline: Apple tightens macOS Full Disk Access controls as AI agents raise new risks
articles.subtitle: Apple says users will have to take 'very explicit action' before an app can read their files, mail, messages and browsing history, warning that the risks grow substantially as agents become more autonomous.
articles.body:
Apple has announced new controls around macOS's Full Disk Access permission, warning that increasingly capable AI agents make broad access to a user's files, messages, Mail and browsing history riskier. In a post aimed at developers, the company said some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems «without users' full knowledge and understanding».

Under the changes, users who «genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access» will be able to do so only with «very explicit user action». Apple said addressing this is «critical» because the risks «will grow substantially» as agents become more capable and autonomous, and noted that the permission was designed so that backups could function properly.

## The disputes behind the change

The move follows an Inc. column by Jason Aten, who reported that Meta's Muse agent knew the contents of his private messages even though he says he never gave it permission; Meta disputes that account. Days earlier, a Wired report said a flaw in ChatGPT's Mac app could have let hackers grab sensitive data.

Desktop agents lean heavily on this setting. In Muse's case, users can optionally enable Full Disk Access, which gives an app permission to read files, mail, messages and browsing history. Apple did not respond to TechCrunch's question about the change.

articles.headline: Epic pauses product development for six weeks after an AI model found a hidden MyChart flaw
articles.subtitle: The medical-records giant says some customer configurations of MyChart could let outsiders read patient records without leaving a trace in the logs. Anthropic's frontier cybersecurity model Mythos surfaced the flaws.
articles.body:
Epic, the company behind the MyChart patient portal, has paused product development for about six weeks after a deployment of Anthropic's frontier cybersecurity model Mythos unearthed security flaws that could expose patients' data. Founder and chief executive Judy Faulkner told Modern Healthcare the pause was needed while work continues on «safeguarding» the company's products.

Epic has not disclosed the nature of the bugs, but its chief security officer, Stirling Martin, told The New York Times that some customer configurations of MyChart could allow outsiders to access patient records without recording any intrusion in the software's logs.

MyChart is used to maintain more than 320 million patient records across US hospitals and doctors' offices. Epic says it does not hold customers' medical data, but a bug unknown to the company could let attackers compromise multiple MyChart systems at once.

It is rare for a company to pause development to fix security bugs, but AI tools capable of rapidly finding and exploiting vulnerabilities are raising the stakes. A 2024 ransomware attack on Change Healthcare exposed data on more than 192 million people, and this year has brought breaches at CareCloud, McKesson and Craneware; the largest healthcare breach listed for 2026 so far is a DentaQuest incident affecting 15 million people.

articles.headline: Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery will become Skydance when their $110bn merger closes
articles.subtitle: Paramount CEO David Ellison says the two studios will operate under the name of his own production company. The deal is expected to close on October 6 after a drawn-out battle with Netflix and 12 states.
articles.body:
Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will operate as Skydance once their merger closes, Paramount CEO David Ellison announced on Friday. The roughly $110 billion deal is expected to close on October 6 and takes its name from Ellison's original film production company.

The combination folds together two major Hollywood studios, the streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max, and networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central and the Food Network. Skydance will also control franchises such as The Lord of the Rings, Game of Thrones, the DC Universe and Yellowstone.

The merger followed a drawn-out corporate battle. Netflix had agreed to acquire Warner Bros.' streaming and studio businesses before the broader Paramount deal moved forward. Twelve states challenged the deal, arguing it could reduce competition and harm consumers and workers, but a judge approved a settlement with the state attorneys general this week.

Ellison said the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands will remain central. «We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one», he wrote on X, adding that the new name gives the company «an identity of its own» while letting both studios «remain in the spotlight».

articles.headline: Rivian sets a delivery record as the R2 ramps up, then recalls it over battery fasteners
articles.subtitle: The EV maker delivered 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter, up 45%, and produced 19,751. The same week it issued a second R2 recall because fasteners on the high-voltage battery pack may not be tightened properly.
articles.body:
Rivian reported its strongest quarter yet, building 19,751 vehicles and delivering 19,248 in the three months to 30 September — an 85% rise in production and a 45% jump in deliveries year on year. The company reaffirmed guidance of 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries for 2026.

The surge is a rare bright spot in a struggling market. US EV sales were down nearly 24% year on year as of September, according to Cox Automotive, a year after the $7,500 federal tax credit was scrapped; Tesla reported a 2.1% fall in quarterly sales. Rivian's more affordable R2 is meant to carry the company to profitability.

The same week brought a second recall for the R2. Rivian found that fasteners on its high-voltage battery pack might not be properly tightened, which can cause a loss of power while driving. Only around 14 vehicles may be affected, and the company says it is not aware of any crashes or injuries.

A manufacturing operator at Rivian's Normal, Illinois plant noticed an under-torqued fastener on 17 September; the company investigated and reprogrammed the automated station to reject them. Rivian has said it plans to ship 20,000 to 25,000 R2s by the end of the year, which would make it one of the fastest launches of a new EV in the US.

articles.headline: ICE agents flagged protest observers in a Palantir-built database, court filing alleges
articles.subtitle: A redacted filing made public on Friday says one DHS agent created records on people watching immigration arrests in Maine, shared their photos for facial recognition and warned an observer of a 'domestic terrorism watchlist'.
articles.body:
US immigration agents flagged people who observed enforcement operations in a database built by Palantir, according to a court filing made public in redacted form on Friday. The filing alleges that agents intimidated protesters and observers by driving past their homes and, in one case, requiring an observer to be sent to secondary inspection at the border until at least January 2027.

It focuses on «Operation Catch of the Day», an immigration enforcement surge in Maine in January, and is part of a proposed class action brought by four observers. One Homeland Security agent, named in the filing as Agent J.C., created case records on at least six observers, according to the filing; the government puts the number at eight.

## A facial recognition request

J.C. labelled two people he filmed in a Home Depot car park «Threat to Law Enforcement, Professional Protestor», the filing says, and sent photos to a Customs and Border Protection officer to run through a facial recognition app called Mobile Query. Records created in the Investigative Case Management system, which Palantir built for ICE in 2014, are automatically shared with CBP watchlists used to screen travellers.

The Department of Homeland Security calls the case «meritless» and denies keeping a database of domestic terrorists; it argues the incidents were isolated and that its policy prohibits such conduct. Protect Democracy, which represents the observers, says the government is treating people exercising First Amendment rights as criminal suspects.

articles.headline: Meta open-sources the hardware code for Muse gadgets, starting with a free Home Link
articles.subtitle: The project gives developers open-source firmware and a Linux SDK so they can build their own devices that connect to Meta's AI agent, from e-ink displays to a stick that plugs into a TV.
articles.body:
Meta has introduced Muse Gadgets, an open-source project that lets developers build their own hardware connected to its AI agent, Muse. The company is providing open-source firmware, a Linux software development kit and a few project ideas, including giving Muse a colour e-ink display or loading it onto a stick that plugs into a television's HDMI port.

There appear to be few limits. Users can set up a low-cost hobbyist computer such as a Raspberry Pi or an off-the-shelf ESP32 board and connect Muse «to your displays, buttons, sensors, actuators, and whatever else you've got lying on your workbench», Meta notes. The company has also opened a Discord channel for support.

## Free Home Links

Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta's Superintelligence Labs, said Meta built a gadget of its own: Muse Home Link, a USB-C-powered device that connects Muse to a home network so it can talk to smart speakers, televisions and other devices. Meta made 5,000 of them and is giving them away free to Muse subscribers while supplies last, with shipping expected in a few weeks.

Muse Gadgets is unlikely to have mass appeal, but it fits Meta's strategy of making Muse more than a standalone chatbot. The company this week also launched Muse for Small Business, which links the agent to Shopify, Dropbox and Slack, and a new Meta Enterprise Platform unit aimed at corporate customers.

articles.headline: Ataraxos beats the world's best Stratego player, and cost a few thousand dollars to train
articles.subtitle: The AI, built by researchers at Carnegie Mellon, MIT, NYU and Stanford, beat Pim Niemeijer 15 games to one. It needed 16 GPUs, while DeepMind's DeepNash soaked up 1,024 chips.
articles.body:
Deep Blue beat Garry Kasparov at chess and AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go, but Stratego held out: even DeepMind could not reliably beat the best human players. A team from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, NYU and Stanford has now done it. Their AI, Ataraxos, beat Pim Niemeijer — arguably the best Stratego player of all time — 15 games to one, with four draws.

Stratego hides a huge amount of information that unfolds over a long game: each side has 40 pieces whose identities are revealed only in battle, giving more than a decillion possible setups, and a match can last 2,000 moves. Earlier machines such as DeepNash struggled both to learn in that setting and to bluff convincingly.

## Learning to guess

Ataraxos trained on 163 million self-play games and added something DeepNash lacked: a second neural network that guesses the opponent's hidden pieces from how they have been moving, so it can sample plausible layouts instead of iterating through all of them. It learned from roughly 34 times fewer games than DeepNash and still ended up stronger.

The price tag is the headline. DeepNash ran for two to three months on 1,024 specialised Google chips, an estimated $3m to $4.5m at 2025 prices; Ataraxos needed 16 GPUs for a week, plus four more for four days to train the belief model. The same architecture also beat champions at Barrage Stratego and topped the best bots at the Chinese card game dou dizhu.

articles.headline: An AI video of a dead victim got a US killer's sentence thrown out
articles.subtitle: An Arizona appeals court ruled that the AI-generated clip, in which the victim appeared to forgive his killer, crossed a line and should not have been shown. The manslaughter conviction stands.
articles.body:
An Arizona road rage killer will be resentenced after an appeals court ruled that an AI-generated video message from his dead victim was improperly aired in court. Gabriel Paul Horcasitas was found guilty of shooting and killing Christopher Pelkey, 37, during a confrontation at a red light in 2021, and was sentenced to 10 years; the court upheld the manslaughter conviction but vacated the sentence in a decision released on Wednesday.

His legal team argued the trial judge should not have allowed the video, created by Pelkey's family, to be shown ahead of last year's sentencing. The court agreed that the clip was not reliable and «crossed that line», writing: «Rather than document an event or recording a particular moment, the AI video presents a depiction of the victim and his thoughts created from the imaginings of the victim's sister».

The sentence is now void and the case returns to the lower court. Prosecutors had argued the footage was an accurate representation of Pelkey's character, and his family has said it is ready to take part in a new sentencing hearing. An attorney for the defendant declined to comment.

The court noted that no Arizona case had previously addressed whether an AI-generated depiction of a victim can be offered as a victim impact statement, making this the first appellate ruling of its kind in the state.

articles.headline: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 lets you compose an image with bounding boxes
articles.subtitle: The new image model adds native layout control — you draw a box for each element and describe what goes inside it — plus multi-reference composition and edit-at-once workflows.
articles.body:
Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3 Image, an image model built around what the company calls maximum control over every pixel. Its headline feature is layout by bounding box: you draw a box for every element that matters and describe what belongs inside it, and the model renders the scene with each element placed where you put it.

The company says a prompt upsampler turns a short request into the dense caption the model was trained on. The upsampler may suggest extra elements, but every box reaches the model verbatim, with the same id and coordinates. Bounding boxes suit compositions with many parts in strict relationships: type set around a photograph, collages and panel grids, or a crowded scene where every face has its place.

## References and edits

FLUX 3 can also take up to 10 reference images, each with its own token, and decide where each one sits and how big before rendering the whole frame. A separate workflow allows multiple targeted edits at once: re-describe one part of a picture, replace an object or recolour something, while everything outside the box stays locked and unchanged.

The model is available through the BFL API and a playground where boxes can be drawn by hand, and Black Forest Labs is pitching it at designers who need precise, repeatable layouts rather than one-off generations.

articles.headline: Trump's 'super intelligence' rebrand sends Slovenia's .si domains surging
articles.subtitle: Registrations of the country's domain overtook .ai in the 25 hours after Trump told the UN that artificial intelligence should be called 'super intelligence'. Many buyers are speculators in the US and India.
articles.body:
Donald Trump's push to rebrand artificial intelligence as «super intelligence» has had an unlikely beneficiary: Slovenia. Registrations of .si domains overtook .ai in the 25 hours after he told the UN General Assembly on 22 September that the technology needs a new name because «artificial» makes it sound fake.

Registry SI, which manages the country's domains, reported a 2,199% increase in .si purchases during September. It recorded 11,000 new addresses on 30 September, the day after Trump signed an executive order requiring government agencies to use the term, and almost 13,000 more in the following 24 hours.

## From domains to aftermarket

Web host Hostinger says .si is now its second most popular extension after .com, with more than half of buyers coming from the US and India — though only around 3% of the names are explicitly AI-related. Analysts describe a speculative rush: more than 50% of the .si domains Netcraft tracked being bought through Dynadot are already listed for resale.

One founder told TechCrunch he bought the .si version of his company's name «to protect the brand in case this takes off like .ai». The economics differ, though: .si costs about $12 a year, while .ai goes for around $90 and requires a two-year commitment. «For Anguilla, .ai became a second economy. For Slovenia, .si is a nice bonus», one analyst said.
